test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Assume that the value of the cash reserve ratio is 25%. What will be the value of money multiplier?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The value of the **cash reserve ratio** (CRR) is **25%**.
 
• The **money multiplier** is calculated as the reciprocal of the cash reserve ratio.
 
• Formula: **Money Multiplier = 1 / CRR**
 
• Given that CRR is 25%, the money multiplier is calculated as follows:
 
• **Money Multiplier = 1 / 0.25 = 4**
 
• Therefore, the value of the money multiplier is **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **cash reserve ratio** (CRR) is a percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the central bank as reserves.
 
• The **money multiplier** effect describes how an initial deposit can lead to a larger final increase in the total money supply.
 
• A higher CRR means a lower money multiplier and vice versa.
 
• The central bank uses CRR as a tool to control liquidity in the banking system.
